title: Exact-cost record selection
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let the base configuration be a four-tape configuration on input $x$, let $i$ be an index from $0$ through $8$, and let the table be $l\,G\,B\,r$. Suppose $G$ is the concatenation of the serialized records in a list of groups, each containing exactly nine one-work-tape binary machine actions; suppose $B$ is the concatenation of the serialized records of a list of actions of length $i$; and suppose the state tape encodes the number $g$ of groups in unary, with its cursor at $1$. Starting in the record-group phase with index $i$ and table cursor $|l|$, after exactly $2g+|G|+|B|+3$ steps the interpreter is in the action-reading phase at field $0$ with its bit register cleared, table cursor $|l|+|G|+|B|$, and state tape encoding $0$ in unary with cursor $1$; the other configuration data are inherited from the base configuration.

the destructive state count with its rewind costs $2g + 3$.
